plan.contextChunk: This figure is a single horizontal strip in which one camera is repeated five times in a row on a white ground, with thick red arrows between and around the copies. Each camera is a black wireframe viewing frustum in three-quarter view: a solid black dot marks the projection center at the left, four straight edges spread rightward from it to the corners of a tall rectangle standing for the image plane, and a faint vertical line inside that rectangle marks its midline. All five frusta match in size and orientation, and every one opens toward the right. A red arrow lies on the axis left of the first camera, another sits in each gap between consecutive cameras, and a final one continues past the last camera to the right edge; all arrowheads point right. Because the arrows run in the same direction the frusta face, the strip shows a camera moving straight ahead down its own optical axis, the case in which the sideways velocity components vanish and only the component along the Z-axis is nonzero.

elements: five ghost camera frusta (thin grey wireframe) at discrete positions along the +X optical axis, echoing the source strip
one active highlighted camera frustum (black wireframe) that translates continuously along +X
solid black projection-center dot at the apex (left) of every frustum
tall image-plane rectangle at the right of each frustum (perpendicular to the optical axis), drawn as a parallelogram by the receding Z diagonal
faint vertical midline inside each image-plane rectangle
four straight frustum edges spreading from each apex dot to the four corners of its image-plane rectangle

thick red direction arrows lying on the optical axis: one left of the first frustum, one in each gap between consecutive frusta, one continuing past the last frustum, all arrowheads pointing +X (right)
a small cluster of 3D scene points placed in front of the cameras (further +X) spread laterally (Z) and vertically (Y)
projected-point markers on the active image plane that move radially outward from the centre as the active camera advances
optical-axis line running horizontally through the active camera apex
(flow view) a face-on image plane showing a radial outward vector field of red arrows emanating from the centre
(flow view) a focus-of-expansion marker (black dot) at the image-plane centre / principal point

interactions.label: Forward translation
interactions.teaches: As the camera travels straight down its optical axis, every projected scene point slides radially outward from the image centre — pure forward (Z) translation produces an expansion flow field, not a sideways shift

interactions.label: Time t
interactions.teaches: Sweeping time moves the active frustum and the red arrows together along the axis while the frustum's orientation never changes; only the depth to the fixed scene shrinks, so projections grow

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: Switching views links the 3-D rightward frustum motion to its 2-D consequence: a field of vectors pointing outward from the focus of expansion, with magnitude increasing with image radius

demo_steps.title: Discrete strip (t = 0)
demo_steps.narration: The active black frustum sits at the first ghost position; the row of identical frusta and rightward red arrows show a camera sampled at five instants while translating forward along its optical axis.

demo_steps.title: Halfway (t = 2)
demo_steps.narration: The active frustum has advanced to the middle ghost. Orientation is unchanged, but the projected scene points on its image plane have moved noticeably outward from the midline.

demo_steps.title: Near the scene (t = 4)
demo_steps.narration: At the last position the camera is closest to the scene points, so their projections are pushed far toward the image-plane border — the radial expansion is strongest here.

demo_steps.title: Image-plane flow field
demo_steps.narration: The same forward motion, viewed on the image plane alone: every flow vector points away from the central focus of expansion, and vector length grows with distance from centre.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World axes: +X = optical axis / row direction (drawn horizontal-true), +Y = vertical image-plane height (true), +Z = lateral depth (the single receding diagonal of the oblique pose). Ghost frusta apex dots at x = 0, 2, 4, 6, 8; each frustum length ~1.2 so its image plane sits at apex_x + 1.2. Image-plane rectangle ~1.6 tall (Y) by ~1.0 wide (Z). Scene points clustered near x = 12, spread Y,Z within +/-1.5. Projected point on active plane = (Y_s/(X_s - camX), Z_s/(X_s - camX)) * planeScale, so as camX grows the denominator shrinks and the radius grows (expansion). Optical-flow law for translation T=(0,0,Tz): u = x*Tz/Z, v = y*Tz/Z -> radial, magnitude proportional to image radius, focus of expansion at the principal point (centre). Colours: frustum wireframe black #000000, ghost frusta grey #999999, image-plane midline grey #888888, red arrows and flow vectors #e60000, projected/scene points orange #ff8800, focus of expansion black #000000, background white.
interactionPlan.notes: Build each frustum as a THREE.LineSegments group: 4 apex-to-corner edges + 4 rectangle outline edges + 1 vertical midline; clone for the 5 ghosts (grey, static) and one active group (black) whose group.position.x is driven by timeT and the animation. Keep scene points as small spheres fixed in world space; recompute their projected markers on the active plane every frame. For the toggle, keep two top-level groups (stripGroup, flowGroup) and switch .visible rather than rebuilding. Flow view: a face-on plane with ~24-32 red arrows on a polar grid, each arrow direction = radial outward, length proportional to its radius, plus a central black FOE dot. Drive the animation by mapping looped time onto the same timeT range so animation and slider stay consistent.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World axes: +X = optical axis / row direction (drawn horizontal-true), +Y = vertical image-plane height (true), +Z = lateral depth (the single receding diagonal of the oblique pose). Ghost frusta apex dots at x = 0, 2, 4, 6, 8; each frustum length ~1.2 so its image plane sits at apex_x + 1.2. Image-plane rectangle ~1.6 tall (Y) by ~1.0 wide (Z). Scene points clustered near x = 12, spread Y,Z within +/-1.5. Projected point on active plane = (Y_s/(X_s - camX), Z_s/(X_s - camX)) * planeScale, so as camX grows the denominator shrinks and the radius grows (expansion). Optical-flow law for translation T=(0,0,Tz): u = x*Tz/Z, v = y*Tz/Z -> radial, magnitude proportional to image radius, focus of expansion at the principal point (centre). Colours: frustum wireframe black #000000, ghost frusta grey #999999, image-plane midline grey #888888, red arrows and flow vectors #e60000, projected/scene points orange #ff8800, focus of expansion black #000000, background white.
interactionPlan.notes: Build each frustum as a THREE.LineSegments group: 4 apex-to-corner edges + 4 rectangle outline edges + 1 vertical midline; clone for the 5 ghosts (grey, static) and one active group (black) whose group.position.x is driven by timeT and the animation. Keep scene points as small spheres fixed in world space; recompute their projected markers on the active plane every frame. For the toggle, keep two top-level groups (stripGroup, flowGroup) and switch .visible rather than rebuilding. Flow view: a face-on plane with ~24-32 red arrows on a polar grid, each arrow direction = radial outward, length proportional to its radius, plus a central black FOE dot. Drive the animation by mapping looped time onto the same timeT range so animation and slider stay consistent.

plan.authoredPrompt: This figure is a single horizontal strip in which one camera is repeated five times in a row on a white ground, with thick red arrows between and around the copies. Each camera is a black wireframe viewing frustum in three-quarter view: a solid black dot marks the projection center at the left, four straight edges spread rightward from it to the corners of a tall rectangle standing for the image plane, and a faint vertical line inside that rectangle marks its midline. All five frusta match in size and orientation, and every one opens toward the right. A red arrow lies on the axis left of the first camera, another sits in each gap between consecutive cameras, and a final one continues past the last camera to the right edge; all arrowheads point right. Because the arrows run in the same direction the frusta face, the strip shows a camera moving straight ahead down its own optical axis, the case in which the sideways velocity components vanish and only the component along the Z-axis is nonzero.
plan.authoredInteractions:
- Animation for advancing the camera copies along their optical axis; the frustum moves straight through the scene while projected points expand from the image center, linking forward Z translation to radial optical flow.
- Slider for time along the forward path; the active camera position and red direction arrows update together, showing that orientation stays fixed while depth to the scene changes.
- Toggle between the 3-D camera strip and the corresponding image-plane flow field; the visible update switches from rightward frustum motion to outward vectors, clarifying how forward translation becomes expansion in the image.
